newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Richter reports rising sales to all mkts.
newsitem.headline: Richter reports rising sales to all mkts.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Richter Gedeon Vegyeszeti Gyar Rt said its total sales rose by 35.3 percent in the January-September period over the same nine months of 1995 with increases in each of its markets.

"Increases were achieved in each of the company's four main geographical areas - Hungary, Commonwealth of Independent States, Eastern Europe and the rest of the world," Richter said on Thursday in its result report.
Richter, releasing its IAS results for the first nine months of 1996, said its total sales amounted 26.608 billion forints compared to 19.67 billion in the same period of 1995.
Richter's net profit soared to 9.023 billion forints in the January-September period from 6.28 billion in the corresponding period of 1995.
The company's domestic sales reached 8.555 billion forints, a 34.8 percent rise over the same period of 1995, it said.
"As in previous quarters this year, the increase was mainly due to the growth in sales of the newer products, particularly Ednyt and Quamatel," Richter said.
The company said it retained its second place ranking in the Hungarian pharmaceutical market and its market share continued to exceed nine percent during the period.

Richter's nine-month sales to the former Soviet Union, excluding the Baltic States, rose to 7.585 billion forints from 5.478 billion forints in the same period of 1995, with the increase coming entirely from direct sales because no tender business was conducted, it said.
"A steady increase in sales for the first nine months of 1996 was reported by the Ukraine where economic conditions continue to improve," Richter said.
"In Russia the company continued to work satisfactorily with its partner on the development of its recently established joint venture manufacturing and warehousing facilities."

"The strong distribution network continues to be a positive contributor to the company's market presence and whilst the general political and economic conditions remain uncertain, trading conditions remain stable," Richter said.
Richter's eastern European sales, including the Baltic States, grew to 3.89 billion forints from 2.788 billion.
Particularly strong growth was reached on a relatively low base in the Baltic states where the company opened its office late last year, Richter said.
The company's sales to what it calls the rest of the world rose to 6.578 billion forints from 5.058 billion.
On Wednesday on the Budapest Stock Exchange Richter shares closed at 8,370 forints, up 110.
